newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit down slightly, but stays in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit down slightly, but stays in narrow range.

text.p: The ringgit was in a narrow range throughout the day, first retreating slightly on continuous selling pressure and then recovering as the market squared up, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said the ringgit looked set for further gains in the near-term as the market was still long dollar.

"There are also some late (dollar) sales out of KL from exporters, while those who have been buying (dollar) are squaring up their positions," said the head of spot foreign exchange dealing at a foreign bank in Kuala Lumpur.
"At the moment dollar still looks on its way down, but in the longer-term it should be gaining against ringgit," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
Dealers said ringgit buying had resumed after Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's statement on Tuesday that he did not want the ringgit to weaken.
Mahathir told reporters at an energy conference that he didn't "see the need to lower the ringgit".
At 0830 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5020/23 per dollar against 2.5021/26 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
